name: Self-employed (England, Wales & Northern Ireland)
appliesTo: Self-employed people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland

items.label: Class 4 National Insurance
items.note: Self-employed National Insurance on profits: 6% between £12,570 and £50,270 and 2% above. Paid through Self Assessment, not PAYE. Class 2 is treated as paid on profits of £7,355 or more, so there's nothing to pay.

assumptions: Self-employed sole trader: the figure is taxable profit, after allowable expenses
No other income, and nothing already paid through PAYE
Profits of £7,355 or more, so Class 2 National Insurance is treated as paid
No student loan or pension contribution unless one is chosen
notModelled: Voluntary Class 2 contributions (£3.80 a week) on profits under £7,355
Higher-rate relief on personal pension contributions, which is claimed through Self Assessment
Trading allowance, losses, capital allowances and other adjustments to profit
When the tax is paid: payments on account are worked out separately on the self-employed pages

sources.title: HMRC — Budget 2026: Overview of tax legislation and rates, Annex A (Class 2 and Class 4 for 2027 to 2028)

obtainedFrom.title: OOTLAR Annex A, read 26 Nov 2026
obtainedFrom.note: 2027/28: Class 4 6% between £12,570 and £50,270, 2% above (unchanged); Class 2 Small Profits Threshold £7,355; voluntary Class 2 £3.80 a week.

obtainedFrom.title: Self-employed National Insurance rates (GOV.UK)
obtainedFrom.note: Read 16 Nov 2026, tax year 2026 to 2027: Class 4 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270 and 2% over £50,270; Class 2 treated as paid on profits of £7,355 or more, voluntary £3.80 a week below that.

tests.note: Below the personal allowance and the lower profits limit: nothing to pay.
